sections.title: Sound of S
paragraphs: The letter (S) /ʃ/ makes two sounds. Its main sound is a hiss. You hear it in the word (sun) /sʌn/, which means the star that gives light to Earth. It can also sound like a buzzing bee.

sections.title: How to say S
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip near the tooth ridge. Blow air through the narrow gap. Keep your voice off. Put your hand on your throat. You feel no shake. For the second sound, make the same hiss. Turn your voice on. Now your throat shakes.

sections.title: Spelling of S
paragraphs: At the start of words, this letter makes the voiceless hiss in (sun) /sʌn/. It makes the same hiss before voiceless consonants, as in (stop) /stɒp/. Between vowels, it becomes voiced in (rose) /roʊz/ and (busy) /bɪ.zi/. The letter is a silent letter before l in (island) /aɪ.lənd/.

sections.title: Comparing S
paragraphs: Do not turn the voiceless hiss into a voiced buzz too early. In words like (sun) /sʌn/, keep your vocal cords quiet. Do not add a vowel before the letter. When a word starts with two consonants, do not say an extra vowel sound at the front.
